 This Writ Petition Coming On For Hearing On I.A.,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

R.DEVDAS J., (ORAL):
Though the matter is coming up for hearing on interlocutory application, with the consent of the learned counsels on both the sides, the matter is taken up for final disposal.
2. The petitioner is a partnership firm running the business of cold storage in Plot No.1318 at Autonagar, Kanabaragi, Belagavi City in the name and style of "Seven Star Group".

The petitioner is before this Court assailing the order of seizure of meat from the petitioner's premises and subjecting the same to P.F.No.30/2018 dated 01.03.2018 on the file of JMFC-II Court, Belagavi pursuant to case registration at Mal Maruti Police Station in Crime No.45/2018.
3.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has produced copy of orders passed in W.P.No.102964/2018 dated 28th June, 2018 and W.P.No.102915/2018 dated 26th April, 2018.

The learned counsel submits that under similar circumstances, the Co-ordinate Benches of this Court have analysed the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and held that it is the Commissioner of Food Safety who has to decide, as per the gravity of offence, whether the matter could be referred to a Court of ordinary jurisdiction or a special Court.
It was further held that it is only thereafter that criminal action for prosecution against an alleged violator of the license or regulations under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 commences.

It was therefore held that under the facts and circumstances of the case, the provisions of Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006 was completely ignored and the Authorities under the Act were neither involved nor intimated before proceeding to seize the goods from the petitioner's establishments.
Consequently, it was held that the action of the police is not in consonance with the provisions of law.
Consequently, the alleged seizure of meat from the business premises of the petitioner and subjecting it to property form before the Jurisdictional Magistrate cannot be sustained.

Although the respondent-police seized the goods from the business premises of the petitioner and seized properties were shown to be subjected to property form before the learned JMFC-II, Belagavi, the Co-ordinate Benches in the cases mentioned supra, desisted from passing any order of quashing of criminal proceedings before the learned Magistrate Court.

The petitioners were granted liberty to make necessary application before the Jurisdictional Magistrate for release of the property and interim custody to the petitioners, in which event, it was also directed that the Jurisdictional Magistrate would invariably go through the observations made by the Co- ordinate Bench in that order.
4. Heard the learned Addl. Government Advocate on behalf of the respondents.

sentences.text: On going through the decision rendered by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court, this Court is in respectful agreement with the decision of the Co- ordinate Bench and therefore similar orders are passed in this matter also.

6. Liberty is granted to the petitioners to make necessary application before the Jurisdictional Magistrate for release of the properties, for interim custody to the petitioner and to remove the seal put on the premises of the petitioner.
In such event, the learned Magistrate Court would invariably go through the observations made before this Court in W.P.No.102964/2018, as stated supra.
With this, the petition stands disposed of.
No order as to costs.
7. In view of the main petition being disposed of, the interlocutory application does not survive for consideration.
